question: to the Commission Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE) Subject:

In April 2024, a Russian citizen left Italy with her two-and-a-half-year-old daughter without the consent of her Italian father. As a result, a criminal case for international child abduction is pending before the Court of Turin. The father filed a report and initiated the procedure laid down in the 1980 Hague Convention to secure the child’s return. According to the same sources, the application was rejected by the Russian courts at two instances. As a result, the father can only maintain contact with his daughter if he travels to Russia. The Hague Convention, applicable between Italy and the Russian Federation, aims to secure the prompt return of children who are wrongfully removed or retained and to ensure that children can maintain contact with both parents. In view of the above: 1.
Is the Commission aware of this case and of the difficulties EU citizens encounter when trying to ensure that the Convention is properly implemented in the Russian Federation?
What cooperation instruments can be used to assist Member States and citizens caught up in international child abduction cases involving third countries?
What is its view of the way in which the Russian Federation implements the Convention and has it encountered repeated difficulties in that regard?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (21.9.2026) The Commission is not aware of the individual case referred to in the question. Relationships between an EU Member State and a third country that are both parties to the 1980 Hague Child Abduction Convention1 are governed by that Convention, not by EU law. Italy and Russia are both Contracting Parties to this Convention, which seeks to protect children from wrongful removal and retention across borders by securing their prompt return and ensuring the protection of rights of access. The application of the Convention is monitored by the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH), not the Commission. EU citizens can ask for assistance from their Central Authority responsible for the application of the Hague 1980 Child Abduction Convention. In Italy, the Ministry of Justice acts as the Central Authority2.
1 The Convention of 25 October 1980 on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction. 2 Ministero della Giustizia, Dipartimento per la Giustizia Minorile e di Comunità; Via Damiano CHIESA No 24
